newsitem.title: CHINA: China to sack coal mine directors for accidents.
newsitem.headline: China to sack coal mine directors for accidents.

text.p: China will sack directors of coal mines if accidents in their mines kill 10 or more people to try to boost safety in China's poorly regulated and often dangerous mines, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.
The tougher penalty is part of a decision by the Ministry of Coal Industry to launch a nationwide safety inspection of coal mines, it quoted Minister Wang Senhao as saying at a meeting on Monday.
The director of a coal mine will be sacked if one accident kills 10 or more persons, and the director of a mining administration will be dismissed if two such accidents occur, Wang said.
The ministry has already ordered a group of coal mines that failed to meet safety standards to limit or halt production, he said.
A total of 30,000 gas alarms will be installed in China's mines this year, he said.

In China's most recent accident, a gas explosion this month at a coal mine in eastern Shandong province killed 31 miners. State media blamed the explosion on the mine's ventilation system, which it said was below standard.
China has issued a string of directives to try to improve safety in its mines where explosions and accidents, mainly at improperly maintained village level mines, kill up to 10,000 miners each year.
